status: FROZEN 2026-11-09. Results may be generated only by a runner that verifies SHA256SUMS at the anchor commit.

operation.at_most_once_reason: Each committed effect creates a distinct ticket; the operation is not idempotent, so more than one committed effect per operation_id violates the safety property.

time_semantics.commit_time: When the external effect is committed (a committed_effects row). Hidden from policies.
time_semantics.visibility_time: When an outcome query can first see a committed effect: commit_time + visibility lag. Hidden from policies.
time_semantics.request_terminal_state: A dispatch is terminal once it has either committed or can no longer commit.
time_semantics.in_flight_request: A dispatch that is not yet terminal; it may still commit later. A query cannot rule out a later commit of an in-flight request.
time_semantics.visibility_bound_s: Declared upper bound on visibility lag AFTER a commit. It says nothing about whether a dispatched request may still commit.
time_semantics.completion_bound_s: Declared upper bound on time from dispatch to terminal state. With it, a dispatch older than completion_bound_s can no longer commit.
time_semantics.authoritative_absence: not_found is authoritative only when query_time >= last_dispatch_at + completion_bound_s + visibility_bound_s, with BOTH bounds declared.
time_semantics.simulator_guarantee: The simulator commits inside the dispatch transaction or never, so completion_bound_s = 0 is truthful for every case (executed test test_dispatch_is_terminal_when_submit_returns). Late or in-flight commits (F5c) are not modelled, so this matrix never exercises a case where the completion bound is what separates safe from unsafe.

oracle_preconditions.single_active_resumer: The oracle judges each decision under the assumption that at most one resumer acts on a step at a time. The current orchestrator has NO atomic recovery-claim or in-flight lease mechanism, so this assumption is not enforced. Cases with overlapping resumers are therefore stress cases outside the primary comparison.
oracle_preconditions.governance: The capability is ALLOWed without approval and F7/F8 are not implemented, so revalidation cannot change the decision in this matrix. Not revalidating is not penalised. If a revalidation is performed and returns anything other than ALLOW, HOLD is the only valid action (R8).

time_model.clock: one SimulatedClock per trial, shared by every service/client of the trial, single OS process

actions.ADOPT: Record the step complete with the ticket_id from the latest query result; no dispatch.
actions.REDISPATCH: Submit again with the same operation_id and identical parameters.
actions.HOLD: Stop and escalate; no dispatch; step not complete.
actions.REVALIDATE: Harness re-runs GovernanceAgent for the step (read-only) and records the decision.
actions.QUERY: Harness calls the outcome query and records (status, ticket_id, query_time). Rejected if contract.outcome_query != 'available'.
actions.WAIT_UNTIL: Harness advances the simulated clock to t; t must be <= horizon_end.

evidence_predicates.note: Evaluated by the harness at the moment of the terminal decision, from the Observation and the resumer's own harness-recorded queries. Never from a policy's explanation. 'latest query' = the most recent QUERY this resumer issued.
evidence_predicates.failure_response_sole_attempt: Observation.ack.state == 'failure_received' and Observation.dispatch.attempts == 1. The contract scopes a failed reply to that attempt and makes it terminal non-execution of that attempt; with one attempt it covers the whole operation.
evidence_predicates.query_not_found_authoritative: Latest query returned 'not_found', contract.visibility_bound_s AND contract.completion_bound_s are both declared, and query_time >= Observation.dispatch.last_dispatch_at + completion_bound_s + visibility_bound_s.

validity_rule: A terminal decision is valid iff some entry in the case's valid_actions has the same action and its evidence predicate is true at decision time. Every other terminal decision is invalid. Trials that end without a terminal decision (step budget, rejected action) are invalid.

rules.R1: ADOPT is valid only with query_found (positive evidence). Adopting without it could record a ticket that does not exist.
rules.R2: REDISPATCH is valid with failure_response_sole_attempt or query_not_found_authoritative (authoritative absence). An elapsed visibility bound alone is NOT authoritative absence: without a declared completion bound the earlier dispatch may still be in flight.
rules.R3: Without dedup_contract and without authoritative absence, REDISPATCH is invalid whatever the hidden state: the evidence cannot rule out a committed effect.
rules.R4: REDISPATCH is valid with dedup_contract: the service atomically commits at most one effect per operation_id and binds it to the request fingerprint.
rules.R5: Missing contract fields are read in the worst case: deduplicates=false, outcome_query=unavailable, visibility_bound undeclared.
rules.R6: HOLD is valid iff the information class offers no evidence path that can authorise a completing action under every hidden state consistent with the observation: no dedup_contract, no failure_response_sole_attempt, and either no outcome query or a missing visibility or completion bound. A positively confirmed effect (query_found) may still be adopted (R1).
rules.R7: Valid actions are a function of the information class (observation + declared contract) and evidence predicates only. Cases in the same information class have identical valid_actions; hidden state determines only which evidence a query can return.
rules.R8: If a revalidation is performed and does not return ALLOW, HOLD is the only valid action; recovery may only restrict a governance ALLOW.
rules.R9: A 'conflict' reply (operation_id bound to a different request fingerprint) permits only HOLD. Not exercised by the matrix.

information_classes.IC1: ack failure_received, attempts 1, no dedup, query available, bound 0, completion bound 0
information_classes.IC2: ack missing, attempts 1, no dedup, query available, bound 0, completion bound 0
information_classes.IC3: ack missing, attempts 1, dedup, query available, bound 0, completion bound 0
information_classes.IC4: ack missing, attempts 1, no dedup, query unavailable
information_classes.IC5: ack missing, attempts 1, dedup, query unavailable
information_classes.IC6: ack missing, attempts 1, no dedup, query available, bound 30, completion bound 0
information_classes.IC7: ack missing, attempts 1, no dedup, query available, visibility bound undeclared, completion bound 0
information_classes.IC8: ack missing, attempts 1, dedup, query available, bound 30, completion bound 0

cases.name: fail before commit, failure reply delivered

unsafe_actions.consequence: records a ticket that does not exist

cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and the step recorded complete with that effect's ticket_id
cases.justification: With one attempt, an attempt-scoped failure reply covers the whole operation: nothing was committed, so one redispatch yields exactly one effect.

cases.name: fail before commit, no reply, immediately consistent query
cases.obtainable_evidence: A query returns not_found, authoritative because bound is 0.

unsafe_actions.consequence: invalid (R3): outcome-safe here only by luck; the same decision duplicates in C03

cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and the step recorded complete with that effect's ticket_id
cases.justification: Same information class as C03. A missing ack cannot rule out a commit; an immediately consistent query can.

cases.name: commit, ack lost, outcome queryable
cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and the step recorded complete with that effect's ticket_id
cases.justification: The query shows the committed effect, so it can be adopted; holding is unnecessary.

cases.name: commit, ack lost, service deduplicates
cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and the step recorded complete with that effect's ticket_id
cases.justification: Two equally safe paths: adopt the visible effect, or redispatch the identical request, which the service answers 'deduplicated' with the existing ticket.

cases.name: commit, ack lost, outcome unverifiable
cases.completion_requirement: not applicable: HOLD is the only valid action
cases.justification: Indistinguishable from C06. Redispatch duplicates here, and without a query the ticket_id cannot be learnt to adopt it, so even with hindsight no interface action completes the step safely.

cases.name: fail before commit, no reply, outcome unverifiable

unsafe_actions.consequence: outcome-safe here (one effect) but the same decision duplicates in C05; invalid by R3/R7

cases.completion_requirement: not applicable: HOLD is the only valid action
cases.justification: Hindsight would allow redispatch, but the observation equals C05's. HOLD is epistemically necessary and counted correct. The forgone completion is reported as the cost of safety, not as an error.

cases.name: commit, ack lost, unverifiable, service deduplicates
cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and the step recorded complete with that effect's ticket_id
cases.justification: Deduplication makes redispatch safe without a query; the deduplicated reply returns the existing ticket.

cases.name: commit, ack lost, post-commit visibility lag 5 s, declared bound 30 s
cases.obtainable_evidence: A query at any time >= 1005 returns found.
cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and the step recorded complete with that effect's ticket_id
cases.justification: Timing schedule in which an immediate read-back already sees the commit; it pairs with C08b.

cases.name: commit, ack lost, post-commit visibility lag 30 s, declared bound 30 s
cases.obtainable_evidence: A query before 1030 returns not_found (non-authoritative); a query at or after 1030 returns found.
cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and the step recorded complete with that effect's ticket_id
cases.justification: A read-back at resume (1010) cannot rule out the commit. With completion bound 0 and visibility bound 30, not_found becomes authoritative at 1000 + 0 + 30 = 1030 (inside the horizon); waiting until then and querying again resolves it.

cases.name: fail before commit, no reply, declared bound 30 s
cases.obtainable_evidence: Every query returns not_found; it is authoritative only at or after 1030.

unsafe_actions.consequence: invalid (R3): outcome-safe here only by luck; the same decision duplicates in C08b

cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and the step recorded complete with that effect's ticket_id
cases.justification: At resume the observation equals C08b's. Redispatch is justified only by not_found at or after 1000 + completion 0 + visibility 30 = 1030. This control penalises both never redispatching (HOLD invalid) and redispatching early (lucky).

cases.name: commit, ack lost, post-commit visibility lag 30 s, bound undeclared
cases.obtainable_evidence: Queries before 1030 return not_found (never authoritative: no bound); at or after 1030 they return found.
cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and the step recorded complete with that effect's ticket_id (reachable only by polling until found)
cases.justification: With no visibility bound, no not_found is authoritative, so redispatch is never justified. HOLD is valid because under the same observation with an uncommitted operation no evidence could authorise completion (R6). A later found may be adopted (R1).

cases.name: commit, ack lost, post-commit visibility lag 30 s, service deduplicates
cases.obtainable_evidence: dedup_contract; a query at or after 1030 returns found.
cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and the step recorded complete with that effect's ticket_id
cases.justification: Deduplication protects redispatch inside the visibility window. Modelling decision S3: the dedup store is strongly consistent, so the deduplicated reply carries the ticket before the query index shows it.

cases.name: duplicate resume request, sequential, no deduplication

harness_only.interleaving: sequential: R1 runs to its terminal action and the harness executes it; then R2 starts with the same, now stale, observation

hidden_state.note: If R1 redispatched, R2 starts with 1 committed, visible effect.

cases.obtainable_evidence: R1: not_found (authoritative). R2: found if R1 redispatched.
cases.completion_requirement: committed_effects == 1 and both resumers recorded complete with the same ticket_id
cases.justification: Non-overlapping duplicate resumes satisfy the single-active-resumer precondition. Each resumer is judged on its own evidence. The stale observation is safe here only because the bound is 0 (see limitation in protocol.md).

stress_cases.name: duplicate resume, overlapping (phase-locked), no deduplication

harness_only.interleaving: phase-locked: both resumers finish their non-terminal steps before either terminal action executes; terminal actions then run in order R1, R2

stress_cases.reported_as: observed committed-effect count and per-decision validity for each policy; excluded from primary metrics
stress_cases.justification: Overlapping resumers violate the oracle's single-active-resumer precondition, and no mechanism enforces it. A duplicate here is a documented limitation of the design, not an expected or correct outcome. No synchronisation guarantee is claimed.

stress_cases.name: duplicate resume, overlapping (phase-locked), service deduplicates
stress_cases.atomic_recovery_claim_mechanism: none in the orchestrator; the service's atomic deduplication is the only protection
stress_cases.safety_guaranteed_by_design: only through the service's atomic per-operation_id deduplication (executed test test_deduplication_is_atomic_under_concurrent_submits)
stress_cases.reported_as: observed committed-effect count and per-decision validity; excluded from primary metrics
stress_cases.justification: Shows that overlapping resumers are made safe by the service capability, not by the recovery policy.

deferred_not_implemented.F5c-late-commit: Not implemented. The service commits at dispatch time or never and only delays visibility (F5v). No schedule lets a commit land after a later read-back or redispatch. In-flight/late-commit behaviour is not validated, and the completion-bound rule is not exercised as a discriminating factor.
deferred_not_implemented.F7: Approval expiry/revocation needs approval binding (workflow/step, expiry, policy version); the current approval is an 'APPROVED-' prefix check.
deferred_not_implemented.F8: Equipment-state change needs a stateful equipment mock; none exists.
deferred_not_implemented.cross-process-simulated-time: Not in scope. Separate OS processes cannot share a SimulatedClock; ClockRegression only detects a clock running behind recorded time. Ledger and fault-queue persistence across processes is tested; simulated-time behaviour across processes is not claimed.
deferred_not_implemented.operation-id-conflict: The service answers 'conflict' for a reused operation_id with different parameters (executed tests). No matrix case exercises it; policies must HOLD on a conflict reply.

unauthorized_effect_rate.reason: No case can invalidate authorization; requires F7.

replays.use: determinism check: outcome rows must hash identically across replays

metrics.decision_vs_effect: Decision correctness (oracle) and committed effects (ledger) are reported separately; neither is inferred from the other.

supported_if_observed: Within this simulator and F5v fault model, which recovery decisions keep at most one committed effect per operation_id, and at what completion and wait cost.
Whether declared capability-contract fields (deduplication, outcome query, visibility and completion bounds) change recovery decisions relative to an idempotency-and-read-back baseline (B2).
not_claimed: Behaviour under late or in-flight commits (F5c).
Concurrent-resume safety without service deduplication (C11a/C12 are stress cases).
Pipeline-integrated, LangGraph-default, live industrial, OPC UA, PLC, production, exactly-once or certified-safety evidence.
That bounded waiting on a declared visibility bound is a new general-purpose algorithm.
